source_clauses: Design a foot pedal for a workbench.
Pressing it should send a signal to the machine.
when I take my foot off it must return to its resting position on its own every time.
It should not move if something brushes against it sideways.

requirements.statement: Pressing the foot pedal must send a signal to the machine.
When the foot is removed, the foot pedal must return to its resting position on its own every time.
The foot pedal must not move if something brushes against it sideways.

scenarios.description: The user presses the foot pedal to send a signal to the machine.
The user removes their foot from the pedal and the pedal returns to its resting position on its own.
Something brushes against the pedal sideways, and the pedal must not move.

actors.name: user
actors.description: The person who presses the foot pedal.

actors.name: machine
actors.description: The entity that receives the signal from the pedal.

actors.name: sideways object
actors.description: An unspecified object that brushes against the pedal sideways.

freedoms: The exact mechanism for sending the signal is not specified.
The means for returning to resting position is not specified.
The design features that prevent sideways movement are not specified.
ambiguities: The specific location of the foot pedal on the workbench is not specified.
The type of signal to be sent is unspecified (e.g., electrical, mechanical).
The definition of 'sideways' is not precisely defined (relative to what axes).
The force or pressure required to press the pedal is not specified.
The pedal's size, shape, or material are not specified.
assumptions: The foot pedal is intended to be operated by the user's foot.
The machine is a separate entity that receives the signal.
The pedal is initially at rest and pressing it is a deliberate action.
